tei:titleStmt.tei:title: אָחִֽינוּ אַתָּה
Aḥinu Ata — a pizmon for a (male) Jew-by-choice's first Aliyah to the Torah after Conversion, by Isaac Gantwerk Mayer

tei:div.tei:head: Aḥinu Ata — a pizmon for a (male) Jew-by-choice's first Aliyah to the Torah after Conversion, by Isaac Gantwerk Mayer

tei:lg.tei:l: Avraham is your father, your mother is Sarah.
You are our brother! You are our brother!
Blessed be the reciever of the yoke of the Torah’s commandments.
You are our brother! You are our brother!
Convert like native, is written in Scripture.
You are our brother! You are our brother!
Dripping covenant-blood for the pure circumcision.
You are our brother! You are our brother!
Entering hei from yod-hei for the cave-purchaser.
You are our brother! You are our brother!
From vav-hei was hei given to the mother and parent.
You are our brother! You are our brother!
Give no oppression, my people, remember, lest he call out!
You are our brother! You are our brother!
How the Mighty and Awesome one cherishes the convert!
You are our brother! You are our brother!
In a pure dipping you cast off your impurity.
You are our brother! You are our brother!
Jewish are you, in happiness and light!
You are our brother! You are our brother!
Kinsman (name: ___) son of Abraham, stand, ascending to the Torah!
You are our brother! You are our brother!

tei:note.tei:p: The parents of all Israel, traditionally stated to be the parents of all converts as well.
M. Sotah 7:8, the declaration of the people Israel when Agrippas, the descendant of converts, came up to read Torah at the haqhel ceremony. This declaration is the refrain of the entire pizmon.

This can refer to a full circumcision or the hatafat dam brit ceremony where a convert who had already been circumcised merely has a drop of blood taken from his penis. This verse would require a major rewrite for a feminine or gender-neutral version. Feel free to suggest your own — remember it has to start with daleth and end with -rah!
Avraham, who was named Avram before his conversion. According to the Zohar, Lekh Lekha 35:454-457, the heis added to Avram and Sarai to make them Avraham and Sarah came from the Divine Name itself.
Sarah, who was named Sarai before her conversion.
Referring to the miqveh that converts go through as part of their process.
